question: What 3-year overall survival did HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer have?

options.E: Survival was not reported by HPV

explanation: Three-year overall survival was 82.4% (95% CI 77.2 to 87.6) for HPV-positive tumours and 57.1% (48.1 to 66.1) for HPV-negative tumours [1].
sourceArticle: Human Papillomavirus and Survival of Patients with Oropharyngeal Cancer

question: After adjustment, the hazard ratio for death with HPV-positive disease was:

options.C: 0.90 for the fractionation comparison, which is a different result

explanation: Adjusted for age, race, stage, tobacco, and treatment assignment, the hazard ratio was 0.42 (95% CI 0.27 to 0.66), a 58% reduction in the risk of death [1].
sourceArticle: Human Papillomavirus and Survival of Patients with Oropharyngeal Cancer

question: What share of the oropharyngeal cancers were HPV-positive?

options.E: Only the HPV-negative cases were tested

explanation: 63.8% of patients with oropharyngeal cancer (206 of 323) had HPV-positive tumours [1].
sourceArticle: Human Papillomavirus and Survival of Patients with Oropharyngeal Cancer

question: How did accelerated-fractionation radiotherapy compare with standard fractionation for 3-year survival?

options.C: Standard fractionation was superior with P < 0.001
options.E: The trial had no fractionation comparison

explanation: Three-year overall survival was 70.3% versus 64.3% (P = 0.18; hazard ratio 0.90; 95% CI 0.72 to 1.13) [1].
sourceArticle: Human Papillomavirus and Survival of Patients with Oropharyngeal Cancer

question: Which other exposure independently worsened survival?

options.D: Use of cisplatin, which was not given

explanation: The risk of death increased significantly with each additional pack-year of tobacco smoking. HPV status remained prognostic after adjustment for tobacco [1].
sourceArticle: Human Papillomavirus and Survival of Patients with Oropharyngeal Cancer
